answer: Per-identity challenges with random jury grading: each key gets a unique prompt each epoch, and its standing decays unless randomly drawn peers keep approving fresh, original work. An attacker growing a grove of fake identities must pay for new judgment for every clone, every round, so cost scales linearly with clones, while similarity checks across the whole ocean of submissions zero out copied or templated answers. A cheap key becomes a canyon of ongoing labor that outweighs any reward.
